target: Yüzde doksan beş başarı oranımız var.
english: We have a ninety-five percent success rate.
tip: Turkish states the percent first: Yüzde doksan beş is literally 'in-hundred ninety-five', meaning 95 percent.

target: Kardeşim benden daha uzun ama ben daha güçlüyüm.
english: My sibling is taller than me but I am stronger.
tip: Comparison uses ablative -den plus daha: benden daha uzun means 'taller than me'.

target: Söz verdim, mutlaka geleceğim.
english: I promised, I'll definitely come.
tip: Söz vermek joins the noun söz (word) with vermek (give) to mean promise, not literally to give a word.

target: Annem bana oda temizletti.
english: My mother made me clean the room.
tip: temizletti is temizle (clean) plus causative -t: make someone clean. bana marks the person who gets made to do it.

target: Marketten ekmek almayı unutmuşum.
english: I forgot to buy bread from the store.
tip: The -muş in unutmuşum marks something noticed after the fact: I seem to have forgotten, not a plain I forgot.

target: Uyumadan önce her zaman okur.
english: Before sleeping, they always read.
tip: uyumadan önce means before sleeping: a verb stem plus -madan önce builds before doing something.

target: Çocuklar okul çıkışında koşarak eve geldiler.
english: The children came running home after school let out.
tip: koşarak is koş (run) plus -arak, meaning by running or while running: it says how the main action happened.

target: Annemin yaptığı börek hiçbir yerde bulunmaz.
english: Nowhere can you find pastry like my mom makes.
tip: Annemin yaptığı means the one my mom makes: -dığı builds a relative clause, and the doer Annem takes -in.

target: Daha dikkatli olsaydık bu hatayı yapmazdık.
english: If we had been more careful we wouldn't have made this mistake.
tip: olsaydık paired with yapmazdık is the past unreal conditional: if we had been, we would not have made it.

target: Ninem her akşam bize bir bilmece sorar.
english: My grandmother asks us a riddle every evening.
tip: sorar uses the aorist -ar for habitual actions, matching her akşam (every evening): things done regularly.

target: Pazartesi sabahı çalar saat çaldığında uyanmak zor.
english: It's hard to wake up when the alarm goes off on Monday morning.
tip: çaldığında means when it rings: add -dığında to a verb stem to say at the time something happens.

target: Yemek pişirmeyi annemden öğrendim.
english: I learned cooking from my mother.
tip: annemden uses the ablative -den to mark the source you learn from: learned from my mother.

target: Bence toplu taşıma ücretsiz olmalı.
english: In my opinion, public transport should be free.
tip: olmalı adds -malı to ol-, meaning should or must be: it states obligation or a firm opinion.

target: İlkbahar gelince soğanları toprağa dikeceğim.
english: When spring comes I will plant the bulbs in the soil.
tip: gelince means once it comes: -ince attaches to a verb stem for as soon as something happens.

target: Belediye yeni parklar ve yeşil alanlar oluşturmaktadır.
english: The municipality is creating new parks and green spaces.
tip: oluşturmaktadır is the formal -makta present: same meaning as -yor but used in official or written Turkish.

target: İstanbul'da vapurla karşıya geçmek keyifli bir yolculuk.
english: Crossing to the other side by ferry in Istanbul is an enjoyable trip.
tip: vapurla is vapur (ferry) plus -la, the by or with ending: by ferry, with no separate word for by needed.

target: Ne kadar çok egzersiz yaparsam o kadar iyi hissederim.
english: The more I exercise, the better I feel.
tip: Ne kadar paired with o kadar frames the more ... the more: Ne kadar çok egzersiz, o kadar iyi.

target: Voleybol yapmaktan hoşlanırım.
english: I enjoy playing volleyball.
tip: hoşlanmak, to enjoy, needs the ablative -tan on what you enjoy. yapmaktan hoşlanırım means enjoy from doing.

target: Otuz günde bu kitabı bitireceğim.
english: I will finish this book in thirty days.
tip: The locative -de marks a timeframe, so otuz günde means within thirty days, not on day thirty.

target: Eskiden insanlar kuyudan su çekerdi.
english: In the old days people used to draw water from a well.
tip: Aorist plus -di makes a habitual past. çekerdi means used to draw, a repeated action long ago.

target: Otobüsü kaçırdı ve yürümek zorunda kaldı.
english: He missed the bus and had to walk.
tip: zorunda kalmak means to be forced to and follows a plain infinitive. yürümek zorunda kaldı means had to walk.

target: Hava ne olursa olsun yarın maça gideceğiz.
english: Whatever the weather, we'll go to the match tomorrow.
tip: ne olursa olsun is a fixed phrase for no matter what. Hava ne olursa olsun means whatever the weather.

target: Çocuklar meyve ve sebze yemeliler.
english: Children should eat fruits and vegetables.
tip: The suffix -meli means should or must, as in yemeliler, they should eat.

target: Daha çok çalışsaydın sınavı geçerdin.
english: If you had studied more you would have passed the exam.
tip: -saydın plus an aorist-past builds an unreal past. çalışsaydın then geçerdin means had you studied, you would have passed.

target: Komşunun tavukları her sabah yumurta bırakıyor.
english: The neighbor's chickens lay eggs every morning.
tip: Possession links two words. Komşunun takes genitive -nun and tavukları takes -ları, the neighbor's chickens.

target: Sahilde toplanan midyeler taze taze pişiriliyor.
english: Mussels collected at the beach are cooked fresh.
tip: Repeating a word intensifies it. taze taze means all fresh or freshly, stressing manner.

target: İstesem de istemesem de bu toplantıya katılmalıyım.
english: Whether I want to or not I must attend this meeting.
tip: The frame -se de and -mese de means whether or not. İstesem de istemesem de means whether I want to or not.

target: Türkçe öğrensem iş bulmam daha kolay olur.
english: If I learn Turkish it will be easier to find a job.
tip: -se on a verb makes an open if. öğrensem means if I learn, with the outcome still possible.

target: Pazardan aldığım çilekler çok taze ve lezzetliydi.
english: The strawberries I bought from the market were very fresh and delicious.
tip: -dığım turns a verb into that I did. aldığım çilekler means the strawberries that I bought.

target: Yolda gelirken kaza gördüm, neyse ki kimseye bir şey olmamış.
english: On the way, I saw an accident, but fortunately no one was hurt.
tip: -ken added to a verb means while. gelirken means while coming, marking the background action.
